closureRule: No P0, P1 or P2 confirmed issue may remain open at product completion.

issues.expected: A child is considered already applied only when Git supplies valid physical evidence.
issues.observed: simple-git resolved merge-base exit 1 with empty stderr and isAncestor returned true for sibling commits.
reproduction: Create base plus sibling commits left/right.
Run native git merge-base --is-ancestor left right (exit 1).
Run the former SimpleGitRunner.isAncestor (returned true).
evidence: historical run e1885451-2d3b-43a2-8b16-5495d4a89fa9 journals marked leaf commits applied while finalSha stayed at base
issues.firstInvariantViolation: packages/execution-core/src/git/runner.ts isAncestor treated a non-throwing simple-git result as ancestry.
issues.rootCause: simple-git error detection does not reject a non-zero exit when stderr is empty.
issues.chosenSolution: Read native merge-base exit code; add physical resultSha evidence, handoff ancestry checks and conservative journal recovery.
rejectedAlternatives: Accept journal state without Git evidence
issues.automatedRegression: Sibling ancestry, corrupt schema-v1 receipt, unexplained crash commit, exact terminal receipt and real Git reentry tests are green.
issues.manualVerification: Native sibling exit 1 reproduced; historical run inspected physically.
residualRisks: Past schema-v1 operations are intentionally failed closed and require a new integration attempt; they are never promoted to success.

issues.expected: A parent consuming a composite receives the composite's complete verified tree.
issues.observed: Only integrationCommitSha (the tip) was cherry-picked; for A'→B' the parent received B's delta and lost A.
reproduction: Integrate sibling leaf commits A and B into a child composite.
Integrate only the child composite tip into a parent from the common base.
Observe b.txt present and a.txt absent.
evidence: tests/integration-real-git.test.ts failed red before fix with a.txt=null
issues.firstInvariantViolation: The synthetic composite result collapsed a multi-commit lineage to a tip without a range/snapshot contract.
issues.rootCause: A single cherry-pick transfers one commit delta, not an arbitrary composite tree.
issues.chosenSolution: Create an explicit merge-shaped handoff whose first-parent diff is the full tree and whose second parent retains the integration lineage; parent cherry-picks mainline 1.
rejectedAlternatives: Range expansion increases journal/repair units and was deferred
issues.automatedRegression: Real nested Git, explicit mainline, handoff shape/tree, redundant patch, physical repair diff and idempotent reentry tests are green.
issues.manualVerification: Handoff has two parents and both files resolve from the parent final SHA.
residualRisks: The handoff is an orchestrator-owned merge envelope and every consumer must preserve its explicit cherryPickMainline=1 metadata; schema and real-Git regressions enforce that contract.

issues.expected: Terminal events reflect the persisted artifact and delivery disposition; completed means verified and delivered.
issues.observed: A failed_artifact run later emitted evidence.ready, approve_merge and run.completed success; artifactOutcome was recorded as unverified instead of failed.
reproduction: Inspect run e1885451-2d3b-43a2-8b16-5495d4a89fa9.
Compare RunRecord failed_artifact with events seq 264-267.
issues.firstInvariantViolation: Event publishing derived terminal success from executionResult.status alone after terminal artifact disposition was already persisted.
issues.rootCause: Execution, artifact and delivery outcomes are conflated in publisher/projection predicates.
issues.chosenSolution: Separate execution, artifact and delivery disposition; require an inspectable non-failed manifest before publishing/projecting evidence; emit terminal success only for a verified delivered manifest; and recover required delivery/terminal facts idempotently from the settled RunRecord.
rejectedAlternatives: Treat execution completed as product completed
issues.automatedRegression: A completed execution with no final artifact persists failed_artifact and emits no run.evidence.ready, approve_merge or run.completed; failed-record projection is equally conservative; verified delivered recovery emits delivery/completion exactly once.
issues.manualVerification: Historical contradictory run and JSONL were compared with the new settled-record predicates; 13 cross-subsystem suites (134 tests) pass.
residualRisks: Legacy contradictory JSONL remains immutable for audit, but run.completed has no reducer mutation and legacy approve_merge gates are durably retired.

issues.expected: There is one functional human confirmation for delivery and it performs a durable, idempotent transition.
issues.observed: approve_merge only appends decision.resolved; /deliver is separate and lifecycle rejects needs_delivery.
reproduction: POST approve_merge on historical run (200).
Observe no RunRecord, receipt, manifest or delivery change.
Check deliver action guard excludes needs_delivery.
issues.firstInvariantViolation: A UI decision advertised merge semantics without owning the delivery side effect.
issues.rootCause: Legacy gate and newer delivery endpoint evolved independently.
issues.chosenSolution: Remove approve_merge from the productive path, retain legacy read compatibility, and make /deliver the sole confirmation from needs_delivery.
rejectedAlternatives: Duplicate delivery safety/CAS inside generic decision route
issues.automatedRegression: Delivery from needs_delivery is lease/CAS guarded, validates terminal preconditions before Git, persists a verified delivered manifest plus required events, returns the same receipt on an identical stale-version retry, and reconciles a crash after Git receipt but before RunRecord persistence. Reused keys with a different request fail closed.
issues.manualVerification: Legacy approve_merge POST behavior was reproduced; the productive route now rejects it and recovery resolves old gates as system-rejected. Real temporary Git repos verify one merge and one receipt.
residualRisks: Delivery is intentionally local Git merge only; remote push/PR delivery remains outside the current product contract.

issues.expected: Each plan revision has one canonical approval decision and one durable resolution; stale revisions cannot approve newer plans.
issues.observed: Live planning raised approve_plan while service resolved approve_plan:r1; recovery synthesized a second resolution.
reproduction: Inspect run e188 events seq 29, 32 and 34.
Trace planning adapter through approval service and recovery.
issues.firstInvariantViolation: The live emitter omitted the plan revision from the decision identity.
issues.rootCause: Decision identity was duplicated as ad-hoc strings across layers.
issues.chosenSolution: Centralize revisioned decision identity, canonicalize legacy r1, and require expectedPlanRevision in approval mutation.
issues.automatedRegression: Live planning emits approve_plan:rN; approval resolves that exact identity; stale rN cannot approve rN+1; edits retire the prior gate and raise the new revision; recovery resolves or rejects legacy/stale gates exactly once.
issues.manualVerification: The historical split identity was traced through emitter/service/recovery; the canonical helper is now the only productive identity constructor and 134 cross-subsystem tests pass.
residualRisks: The bare approve_plan identity is read-only legacy compatibility and is never raised by the productive path.

issues.expected: Every product Git subprocess trusts only the selected repo, using Git-compatible paths and no global config mutation.
issues.observed: Backslash safe.directory was rejected on Windows and provisioning/artifact reads omitted the scoped override.
reproduction: Run Git against cross-owner C:/Users/franc/Desktop/divisorDeGastos with backslash safe.directory (128).
Repeat with forward slashes (0).
evidence: source inventory of direct Git subprocesses
issues.firstInvariantViolation: safeGitArgs used path.resolve output verbatim on Windows.
issues.rootCause: Windows filesystem syntax was passed where Git expects canonical path syntax; wrapper adoption was incomplete.
issues.chosenSolution: Normalize to forward slashes and wrap every direct Git subprocess with the exact repo path.
issues.automatedRegression: Path normalization, provisioning/artifact suites and a static production Git-subprocess inventory guard pass.
issues.manualVerification: Cross-owner read-only rev-parse returned exit 0.
residualRisks: The exception remains intentionally repo-scoped; a newly introduced Git subprocess will fail tests unless it uses safeGitArgs.

issues.expected: One physical repository identity maps to one workspace unless an explicit alias model exists.
issues.observed: Two POSTs with the same repo path create distinct workspaces; legacy store already contains duplicates.
reproduction: POST two workspace names with the same local repo path.
Observe two 201 records and fragmented run histories.
issues.firstInvariantViolation: Repository create/update only checks slug uniqueness.
issues.rootCause: No canonical realpath/case/git-root identity or migration constraint exists.
issues.chosenSolution: TBD after exact/case/symlink/subdir identity tests.
issues.automatedRegression: Missing.
issues.manualVerification: Duplicate records and POST behavior confirmed.
residualRisks: legacy merge policy
Windows case folding
worktree/subdir aliases

issues.expected: D1 dependencies have one explicit end-to-end meaning: they order readiness/dispatch and never imply upstream file materialization.
issues.observed: Planner, executor prompts, UI and system documentation now declare ordering_only; every dependent worktree still starts from graph.baseCommit by design.
reproduction: Plan leaf A creating a schema and leaf B depending on A to read it.
Observe B worktree created from graph.baseCommit.
issues.firstInvariantViolation: The old planner/UI contract implied physical inheritance while the scheduler and worktree layer implemented ordering only.
issues.rootCause: Dependencies were implemented as scheduling constraints only while prompt/product copy promises concrete output availability.
issues.chosenSolution: Formalize D1 as ordering_only across model, decomposer, executor guidance, UI and docs. Concrete predecessor files must remain in one task or be replaced by an explicit sharedInterface; bottom-up integration remains the only physical composition point.
rejectedAlternatives: Materializing predecessor commits into dependent worktrees would weaken isolation, duplicate commits and conflict with bottom-up integration.
Leaving the behavior implicit would continue producing plans that cannot execute as described.
issues.automatedRegression: Real Git proves B's commit parent is graph.baseCommit, B's tree excludes A's file, and integrated output contains both; unit tests guard executor prompt, decomposer prompt and UI copy.
issues.manualVerification: Productive path and copy traced end-to-end; browser rendering remains tracked in E2E-019.
residualRisks: A future physical dependency mode would require a new explicit contract and integration/provenance design; it must not overload D1.

issues.expected: Hierarchy, canonical D1 dependency, seam and conflict edges are distinct and derived from durable facts.
issues.observed: Plan events omit graph.dependencies and seam events are projected as dependency edges; PlanControl and canvas disagree.
reproduction: Open a run with zero D1 dependencies and several seams.
Canvas shows dependency-like arrows while control surface says no explicit dependencies.
issues.firstInvariantViolation: PlanNodeProposed payload/projection has no canonical dependency edge channel.
issues.rootCause: WorkspaceEdge has only hierarchy|dependency and reused dependency for seams.
issues.chosenSolution: Add typed plan.dependency.proposed facts sourced only from canonical graph.dependencies; fold them into RunModel.dependencies; project hierarchy, D1 dependency, seam and active conflict as distinct edge kinds; give task/scheduling, interface and integration lenses explicit visibility channels; and idempotently backfill missing D1 facts in legacy logs from the durable RunRecord.
issues.automatedRegression: Snapshot/live-plan→typed event→reducer→focus/canvas parity, seam/dependency/conflict separation and legacy-log backfill tests pass; 25 run-model/event-log suites (431 tests) and @manyhands/web tsc are green.
issues.manualVerification: Historical e188 seam-only behavior was traced; renderer and lens wiring now consume distinct edge kinds and no seam path writes RunModel.dependencies.
residualRisks: Semantic plan edit removal/revision projection is closed and independently regression-tested under PC-010; it does not change the corrected edge taxonomy or D1 source.

issues.expected: After every semantic edit, RunRecord, revisioned approval and durable UI projection describe the same graph.
issues.observed: The replacement projection fixes cold UI tombstones, but runtime still resolves the unpatched planning graph; approved amendments can resolve their gate before persisting the seam change; replan can overwrite composite roles and late stale structural facts survive recovery.
reproduction: Add/remove a dependency or integrator from PlanControlSurface.
Reload and compare dock snapshot with main canvas.
issues.firstInvariantViolation: Semantic mutation commits without its corresponding durable run-model facts.
issues.rootCause: Snapshot and event log are independently updated, despite UI treating events as authority.
issues.chosenSolution: Keep the typed revision-scoped plan.graph.projected full replacement, then close the remaining authority gaps: execution must resolve the same materialized patched graph; amendment mutation and gate resolution must be ordered behind durable CAS/lease success; replan must preserve projected roles; recovery must supersede any structural fact newer than the last authoritative projection.
rejectedAlternatives: Use mutable snapshot imperatively in canvas
Keep additive-only graph facts and add ad hoc tombstones per entity
issues.automatedRegression: Existing replacement/tombstone and cold reload regressions pass, but review found missing coverage for patched runtime execution, durable amendment mutation, composite role preservation and stale post-projection facts. New red-to-green regressions are in progress.
issues.manualVerification: Read-only trace confirmed four authority/order gaps after the initial projection implementation; Chrome edit/reload verification remains pending.
residualRisks: RunRecord CAS and event append remain an outbox boundary and must be repaired idempotently without consuming a decision before the graph mutation is durable.

issues.expected: Grounded interface seams enable safe parallelism unless concrete files/symbols create risk.
issues.observed: Every producer/consumer seam is unconditionally high risk and serializes tasks, sometimes consumers before producer.
reproduction: Use e188 run with five ready leaves and grounded seams.
Observe three waves and high-risk blocks caused only by producer/consumer relation.
issues.firstInvariantViolation: Seam relation is promoted to high risk before considering grounding or physical overlap.
issues.rootCause: Conflict risk conflates shared interface compatibility with file collision/dependency.
issues.chosenSolution: Treat a canonical compatible sharedInterface as positive compatibility evidence rather than conflict by itself; retain high risk for incompatible declarations and concrete file/import/symbol overlap, and stop duplicating interface IDs into generic expected-output symbols.
rejectedAlternatives: Lower every producer/consumer relation regardless of compatibility or physical overlap
Keep legacy duplicated seam IDs as concrete symbols
issues.automatedRegression: Eight focused suites pass (60 tests): compatible legacy duplicated seams are low/co-scheduled, incompatible declarations remain high, and real concrete symbol/import overlap remains high. Scheduler, conflict-risk and decomposer typechecks pass.
issues.manualVerification: Historical wave selection inspected; a fresh real run proving safe parallel wave selection remains pending in E2E-022.
residualRisks: grounding quality must be explicit before lowering risk

issues.expected: waveId is identity/correlation and humans see a contiguous ordinal 1..N.
issues.observed: Backend persists event sequence as waveIndex; UI renders W46, W139 and W201 for three waves.
reproduction: Inspect e188 wave events and canvas/timeline labels.
issues.firstInvariantViolation: scheduling event adapter overwrites input.waveIndex with seq-1.
issues.rootCause: Correlation position and display ordinal share one field.
issues.chosenSolution: Persist zero-based waveIndex from the count of prior wave_selected facts plus a one-based waveOrdinal, keep waveId for correlation, and derive legacy display ordinals from replay position rather than global event sequence.
issues.automatedRegression: Thirty focused tests pass; synthetic facts at global seq 46/139/201 render and persist human ordinals 1/2/3 across canvas, timeline and chat. Web typecheck passes.
issues.manualVerification: Historical labels confirmed; Chrome verification of the corrected labels remains pending.

issues.expected: Health polling is single-flight, bounded and does not reparse every large RunRecord.
issues.observed: manyhands-dev polls every 2s with 2.5s timeout and no single-flight; corrupt-record scan rereads all JSON files.
reproduction: Run pnpm web:dev.
Inspect manyhands-e2e-web log for sustained /api/runs?limit=5 traffic and overlapping-capable durations.
issues.firstInvariantViolation: Fixed interval schedules a new request before the prior request is guaranteed complete.
issues.rootCause: Dev readiness poll and expensive corruption diagnostics are coupled to the normal list endpoint.
issues.chosenSolution: Replace fixed-interval polling with an immediate self-scheduling single-flight loop and exponential backoff. Decouple the normal list path from corruption crawling through a durable mtime/size diagnostics index: hot polls read only the small cache, real navigation and an explicit diagnostics=refresh request advance a bounded batch.
rejectedAlternatives: Increase the fixed interval while preserving overlap
Reparse every record behind a longer timeout
issues.automatedRegression: Five focused suites pass (24 tests): no overlapping poll is scheduled, failure delays back off/reset, a zero-budget list opens no RunRecord, bounded batches advance and become cache-only, corruption remains discoverable, and the default API route creates no crawl index. Web typecheck passes.
issues.manualVerification: The live existing dev server returned ten normal list requests with nine warm samples between 242 ms and 1.12 s (first HMR compile 6.16 s); explicit bounded diagnostics refresh returned 200 in 1.03 s. Launcher --help loads the new poller successfully.
residualRisks: The layout still enumerates filenames and metadata in bounded refreshes; extremely large run directories may justify a future background service, but normal polling never performs that work.

issues.expected: Product UI exposes only choices executable under the normalized fixed run configuration.
issues.observed: Node override API/UI persists selections that preflight/runtime rejects in fixed routing.
reproduction: Set per-node haiku override on a run fixed to sonnet.
Observe resolveRoutedSelection rejection.
issues.firstInvariantViolation: Control plane accepts a state the product execution policy declares impossible.
issues.rootCause: Legacy complexity-routing controls remain after product default/consolidation to fixed.
issues.chosenSolution: Carry effective routing into the plan control plane. Fixed product runs reject every non-null per-node override in the API and render explicit inherited routing; historical complexity runs retain the selector, and fixed runs can clear legacy metadata with a null mutation.
issues.automatedRegression: Three focused web/control-plane suites pass (30 tests) and web typecheck passes; fixed rejects non-null selections, null clears legacy state, and complexity remains explicitly selectable only for historical runs.
issues.manualVerification: Backend rejection and legacy clear behavior are covered; Chrome verification of the fixed-routing copy/control remains pending.
residualRisks: historical nodes with overrides

issues.expected: UI spacing/type utility classes follow the product scale regression.
issues.observed: Five deterministic spacing offenders in plan-control-surface and app-sidebar after the latest UI changes.
reproduction: Run tests/typography-scale.test.ts.
issues.firstInvariantViolation: New UI utilities bypassed the scale allowlist.
issues.rootCause: Partial UI redesign was not run against typography regression.
issues.chosenSolution: Replace the five 10px p/px utilities with the nearest 4px-scale token (12px / utility 3) without altering component structure.
issues.automatedRegression: Typography scale guard passes (5/5) and web typecheck passes.
issues.manualVerification: Pending Chrome.

issues.expected: Full suite completes deterministically under documented timeout budgets.
issues.observed: run-runner agent-start wait and 500-write checkpointer test time out only under full-suite load.
reproduction: Run full Vitest suite (fail).
Run each test isolated (pass).
issues.firstInvariantViolation: Test timing budgets assume low contention.
issues.rootCause: Two independent load assumptions: the live-start test polled a synchronous controlled seam with a 1s wall-clock budget, while 500 concurrent checkpoint putWrites serialized 500 read/merge/full-rewrite/fsync operations and grew quadratically.
issues.chosenSolution: Synchronize the controlled runner test from an explicit engine-entered deferred instead of elapsed time. Coalesce concurrent pending-write calls per directory/thread/checkpoint under the existing thread write chain, resolving each caller only after its batch is atomically persisted; late arrivals re-arm safely.
rejectedAlternatives: Disable fsync in the durability regression
issues.automatedRegression: Focused runner + checkpointer suites pass under concurrent agent load (20 tests): 500-write test fell from 3.55s isolated to 0.54s under load, and engine-start took 1.44s yet passed because it no longer races a 1s poll. Orchestrator-graph typecheck passes.
issues.manualVerification: Profiled both isolated and under concurrent repository workload; full-suite rerun remains the closure gate.
residualRisks: Full-suite evidence is still required before closure; pending-write batching is process-local while the operation lease remains the cross-process single-writer authority.

issues.expected: A seam connects distinct producer and consumer tasks.
issues.observed: A task can produce and consume ProjectScripts itself, creating a self-edge and hiding unconsumed output.
reproduction: Validate e188 graph/contracts and inspect seam event for project-metadata-and-readme.
issues.firstInvariantViolation: Contract validation accepts producerTaskId === consumerTaskId.
issues.rootCause: Existence is checked but identity separation is not.
issues.chosenSolution: Reject consumed/produced id overlap at the AgentTaskContract executable boundary, surface a blocking self_consumed_seam finding in SeamCritic, instruct the decomposer to use distinct revisioned ids, and filter legacy self-consumers from run-model seam projection.
rejectedAlternatives: Hide the self-edge only in canvas
Treat self-consumption as a valid consumer and suppress unconsumed output
issues.automatedRegression: Five focused suites pass (34 tests): boundary and executable graph reject the shape, critic blocks it and reports output unconsumed, legacy projection has no self-edge, and planner prompt forbids it.
issues.manualVerification: Historical self-seam event traced to the missing cross-field boundary invariant; every productive validation/projection consumer was inspected.
residualRisks: Legacy records retain the invalid raw contract for auditability, but cannot be approved as executable and no longer paint a self-edge.

issues.expected: Only the current operation lease/fencing token can persist integration progress or final evidence.
issues.observed: Journal open/update copies operationId/fencingToken but performs no CAS or stale-writer rejection.
reproduction: Open the same journal with two logical writers and update from the stale token.
issues.firstInvariantViolation: JsonIntegrationOperationJournal.update overwrites by filename without comparing fencing identity/version.
issues.rootCause: The journal predates the repository-wide lease/fencing durability model.
issues.chosenSolution: Schema v2 records source/result/pre-SHA provenance; every transition uses a monotonic CAS revision under a filesystem lock and exact operationId/fencingToken matching.
rejectedAlternatives: Trust caller not to be stale
issues.automatedRegression: tests/integration-operation-journal.test.ts rejects stale versions and mismatched leases; integration recovery tests cover exact terminal receipts.
issues.manualVerification: Journal transitions and first pre-trace CAS claim inspected after implementation.
residualRisks: Filesystem locking is a short critical-section lock; the run operation and task-attempt leases remain the higher-level single-writer authority.

issues.expected: Repair agents never commit; only the orchestrator may create the repair commit after diff/scope/syntax validation.
issues.observed: A repair executor could commit directly, leave an empty staged diff, and have its unauthorized commit propagated by a partial handoff.
reproduction: Create two conflicting child commits.
Use a repair executor that writes forbidden.txt and commits it.
Observe the former flow build a parent-consumable handoff from the executor-owned HEAD.
issues.firstInvariantViolation: attemptRepair did not compare HEAD before and after AgentExecutor execution.
issues.rootCause: The D6 unexpected-commit guard existed for leaf recording but not for semantic integration repair.
issues.chosenSolution: Compare repair HEAD against the orchestrator base, capture Git diff for diagnostics, reject the result, and hard-reset/clean only the managed integration worktree before any partial handoff.
rejectedAlternatives: Drop all prior safe child integrations
issues.automatedRegression: Real Git executor commit is rejected; forbidden.txt is absent, worktree is clean, rogue SHA is not ancestor of the safe partial handoff.
issues.manualVerification: The real regression inspects the final tree and physical ancestry.
residualRisks: Repair always applies the default reject policy; no accept path is exposed for integration agents.

issues.expected: Every executor invocation terminalizes its durable TaskAttempt when it throws or is cancelled.
issues.observed: repairLeaf and integrateComposite could throw after executor_running and leave the attempt ambiguously running.
reproduction: Force RunExecutor.repairLeaf to throw.
Abort while RunExecutor.runNode executes an integrator.
Inspect the task-attempt journal.
issues.firstInvariantViolation: Only the scheduled leaf path caught the executor boundary and persisted a terminal attempt state.
issues.rootCause: Three productive invocation paths implemented error handling separately.
issues.chosenSolution: Centralize thrown-attempt terminalization and wrap scheduled leaf, repair and integration invocation plus result-kind validation.
rejectedAlternatives: Leave running attempts for timeout cleanup
issues.automatedRegression: Repair failure and integration cancellation persist failed/cancelled attempts; related attempt and abort suites pass.
issues.manualVerification: Durable journal assertions inspected.
residualRisks: Later persistence transitions still rely on the run operation lease and their existing CAS guards.
